item.title: Learner Guide
item.description:
This guide takes you through one complete learning journey in the Layer5 Academy: you find a learning path, enroll, work through it, pass its final assessment, and receive your credential. Along the way you learn how the Academy tracks your progress and how its tests are scored, so you know what to expect from any content you take next.

You need a Layer5 Cloud account to enroll. Browsing the catalog needs no account.

item.title: Create a Learning Path
item.description:
A learning path teaches a subject through courses and modules, with assessments that gate progress. You write it as Markdown in your organization’s Academy content repository, then publish a version. This page covers the repository, layout, front matter, assets, preview, and publishing that every Academy content type shares. For the credential and assessment differences, see Build a Challenge and Build a Certification.

Prerequisites 🔗

  • Git, a GitHub account, and Markdown. The Academy is built with the Hugo static site generator.
  • Content registered in the Instructor Console, which gives you the content id and the front matter to start from.
  • Your organization’s ID and a personal access token from Layer5 Cloud, used when you publish. Create tokens as described in Tokens.

Set up the content repository 🔗

Start from the academy-example template repository published by Layer5: github.com/layer5io/academy-example. Fork it, clone your fork, and work on a branch.

item.title: Build a Challenge
item.description:
In Layer5 Academy, a Challenge is a hands-on, scenario-based task. Where a Learning Path teaches a subject from the ground up and a Certification tests knowledge a learner already has, a Challenge gives them a concrete problem and asks them to solve it.

When to use a challenge 🔗

Choose a challenge when the learner should build, break, or fix something real and is scored on the result. Compare the content types in Create Academy Content.

item.title: Create Academy Content
item.description:
Academy content is written as Markdown in your organization’s own Git repository and published as a numbered version. Layer5 Cloud holds the record of each piece of content (its identity, access rules, and badge) and every learner’s registration, progress, and test results. This guide covers the workflow end to end. The pages beneath it cover each content type in depth.

Prerequisites 🔗

  • The View Academy Metrics permission in your organization (Academy Admin, Organization Admin, or Provider Admin). See the Instructor Console.
  • An organization with the Academy configured, so the console is not in its “not configured” state.
  • Comfort with Git and Markdown.

The workflow 🔗

  1. Register the content in the console. The content creation flow creates the content record and generates the identifiers and front matter you paste into your repository.
  2. Write the content in your repository, following the layout for its type.
  3. Preview locally to check structure and links.
  4. Publish by releasing a version of your repository. The release asks Layer5 Cloud to build your organization’s Academy at that version.
  5. Monitor registrations, completion, and pass rates in the console.

Register content in the console 🔗

The creation flow collects the following. Only the content type is required to create the record. The record starts with status not ready, public visibility, and beginner level. Cloud generates the slug from the content type plus three random words.

item.title: Build a Certification
item.description:
In Layer5 Academy, a Certification is a formal assessment designed to validate a learner’s professional skills in a specific domain. Unlike a Learning Path, which guides a user through a curriculum, a Certification’s primary goal is evaluation.

The successful completion of a Certification results in an official, shareable Certificate of Completion and a valuable badge, signifying a verified level of proficiency.

When to use a certification 🔗

Choose a certification when the goal is to test, not teach. It assumes prior knowledge. Compare the content types in Create Academy Content.

item.title: Instructor Console
item.description:
The Instructor Console reports on your organization’s Academy content and learners. It answers three questions: how many people are learning, how far they get, and which assessments stop them. The console is also where you register new content and manage who can access it.

Availability and access 🔗

Academy
Capability What it does Free Team Designer Team Operator Enterprise
Academy Theoretical Learning A comprehensive learning management system for creators and instructors on how to build, manage, and extend educational content like learning paths, challenges, and certifications. -Not included -Not included -Not included ✓Included
Academy Practical Learning An inclusive, collaborative, hands-on learning environment for students. -Not included -Not included -Not included ✓Included

Opening the console requires the View Academy Metrics permission in the selected organization. Without it, the console shows a missing-permission message that names the permission.

item.title: Add Assessments
item.description:
Assessments gate progress and trigger completion in Academy content. A learner who passes an assessment unlocks the next level of the content, and a learner who passes the final assessment completes the content and receives its badge and, where defined, its certificate. Layer5 Cloud scores every submission on the server and records the result in the learner’s grade history.

This page shows how to write an assessment file and explains how the server treats it. It assumes you have a content repository with a learning path, challenge, or certification.

item.title: Platform Development
item.description:
The Academy is assembled from separate repositories for content, theme, and build. This page shows how to preview content on your machine, how to change the theme and see the result on real content, and how to run a production-like build before you publish. Most authors need only the first workflow. Theme development and end-to-end builds are for contributors to the platform itself.

How the repositories fit together 🔗

Repository Role Who touches it
Content repository, such as the academy-example starter or an organization’s own repository Your learning paths, challenges, and certifications, plus the workflow that announces a new version Content authors
academy-theme Layouts, colors, fonts, and the standard shortcodes. Content repositories import it as a Go module, so you never fork it to author content. Platform contributors
academy-build The Hugo configuration for the production build. It pins the version of the theme and of every content module. Platform maintainers

The path from a content change to a live Academy has three stages:

item.title: Use the Content Template Creator
item.description:
The Content Template Creator is the five-step flow in the Instructor Console that registers a learning path, challenge, or certification and hands you the front matter to start writing it. One run does three things:

  1. Creates the content’s record in Layer5 Cloud, with status not ready, public visibility, and a generated slug.
  2. Creates the invitation that governs who can enroll.
  3. Generates the front matter, the content ID, and the organization ID that tie your repository files to that record.

The record is what learners enroll in, what progress and grades attach to, and what the Instructor Console reports on. The front matter is how your repository declares the same content, so the two must carry the same ID.

item.title: Academy
item.description:
Layer5 Academy is the learning platform built into Layer5 Cloud. Organizations use it to publish structured training on cloud native infrastructure, assess what learners know, and award verifiable badges and certificates. Layer5 Cloud tracks every learner’s enrollment, progress, and test results, and gives instructors a console to measure how their content performs.

Academy is an Enterprise-tier capability. An organization needs an Academy configuration from Layer5 before it can publish its own content.

item.title: Extend the Academy
item.description:
Academy content is Markdown in your organization’s Git repository, built with Hugo into your organization’s Academy. Markdown covers most lessons. When a lesson needs a custom layout, a reusable component, or a live design, you extend the content in your own repository without touching the shared theme.

This page covers what you can extend and the limits of each extension. It assumes a working content repository. If you do not have one yet, start with Create a Learning Path.
